steps: Open Dashboard from the sidebar.
Check the active academic year at the top.
Review pending actions first.
Open the required module directly from the sidebar to finish the work.
documents.note: Treat the dashboard as the starting point every day before opening detailed modules.

documents.answer: Pending actions should be treated like a work queue. Use them to finish drafts, review overdue fee follow-up, complete exam work, and close year setup gaps before the team starts creating new records on top of incomplete work.
steps: Read the item carefully.
Open the related module like Attendance, Academics, or Fees.
Finish the draft, finalize the task, or record the correction.
Return to Dashboard to confirm the pending item has reduced.
documents.note: Do not ignore repeated pending actions because they usually indicate incomplete workflow.

documents.title: How does the active academic year work?

documents.answer: The active academic year is the master workspace for school-admin. Classes, students, attendance, marks, homework, fees, and reports should all follow that year so one school can operate 2026, 2027, and later years separately without mixing daily records.
steps: Open Settings.
Go to Academic Year Setup.
Select the correct year workspace.
Return to the required module and continue working.
documents.note: Always check the year banner before saving important records.

documents.title: How do I create a new academic year?

What is the correct order after switching the year?

Create new year

documents.answer: Create a new academic year from Settings when the school is ready to open a fresh operational cycle. During creation, decide what setup data should move forward, keep old transactional history in the previous year, and confirm the new year before daily work starts.
steps: Open Settings.
Go to Academic Year Setup.
Create the target year such as 2027.
Choose whether to transfer student registration details, classes, teachers, and fee setup.
Keep marks, attendance, announcements, and reports independent unless there is a clear need.
documents.note: Base setup can be copied. Live academic operations should usually stay separate.

documents.title: What student data should be transferred to a new year?

What is the correct order after switching the year?
What is the strict student identity and year enrollment workflow?

Year transfer best practice
documents.answer: Only carry forward durable student identity and registration details unless the school has a special reason to transfer more. Attendance sheets, exam marks, finalized reports, and historical financial activity should remain with the old year so the new year starts clean.
steps: Transfer student identity and registration details.
Transfer class structure only if the school wants to reuse it.
Do not transfer attendance history or exam history into the new year.
Confirm the new class placement and fee setup after transfer.
documents.note: Treat each academic year like a separate operational account.

documents.title: What is the correct order after switching the year?

Working order after year switch
documents.answer: After switching the active year, first verify classes, sections, and enrollment structure, then confirm staff roles and fee configuration, and only after that begin attendance, marks, homework, announcements, and other day-to-day entries in the new workspace.
steps: Switch the academic year.
Confirm class setup and teacher setup.
Confirm student enrollments for that year.
Review fee templates and roles.
Start daily operations like attendance and announcements.
documents.note: If the setup is incomplete, daily modules may look empty or inconsistent.

documents.answer: Student identity should be treated as a master record, while year enrollment should be treated as the operational record for a specific academic year. Attendance, marks, reports, homework, and fees must follow the year enrollment layer so the same student can exist historically across years without module mismatch.
steps: Confirm the active academic year.
Upload or create students for that year.
Use the year-specific roster in Attendance, Academics, and Fees.
Review Student Report to verify the records are attached correctly.
documents.note: If the wrong year is active, student lists may appear missing or mismatched.

steps: Open Students > Upload Students.
Choose the class.
Add rows manually or paste spreadsheet values.
Review each row carefully.
Upload the staged list into the database.
documents.note: Use staging carefully to avoid creating duplicate entries.

documents.answer: Review the existing roster first to avoid duplicate year enrollments, accidental class mix-ups, and unnecessary PIN resets. The safest school workflow is to confirm what already exists in the active year and then upload only truly missing or corrected students.
steps: Open Student Report for the current class.
Review the students already created.
Return to Upload Students.
Add only missing students in the spreadsheet stage list.
Upload once the stage list is verified.
documents.note: Duplicate students create reporting and fee confusion.

documents.answer: Same PIN for all applies only to the rows being staged in the current upload action unless the school explicitly edits existing students later. It is a convenience for bulk onboarding, not a rule that should silently overwrite saved PINs on already created records.
steps: Open Upload Students.
Enable Same PIN for all if needed.
Add the staged rows.
Review the PIN column before upload.
Upload the rows.
documents.note: Use a shared PIN only when the school really wants a common temporary access pattern.

Finalize Attendance should be used only when the sheet is ready to become the official daily record, because finalized entries are expected to drive reports, follow-up, and parent communication.
steps: Use Save Draft while review is still pending.
Use Finalize only after checking all statuses.
If corrections are needed later, reopen the sheet.
Make the changes and finalize again.

Use Mark All Present or Mark All Absent only if the situation truly requires it.
Review exceptions such as late or absent students manually.
Use Reset if the current editor needs to be cleared back to the default state.
documents.note: Bulk actions are fast but should always be followed by a quick review.

Use Student History when a parent, class teacher, or admin wants one student's attendance record.
Compare attendance before raising warnings or attendance concerns.

Confirm the selected class and section.

documents.title: How do receipts, dues, concessions, and reversals work?

Add due
Give concession

documents.answer: Receipts record money collected. Dues add or post payable amounts. Concessions reduce payable amounts based on approved relief. Reversals correct a wrong transaction. Each action should be treated like an accounting event so the fee ledger remains explainable later.
steps: Open the correct student ledger in the active academic year.
Choose the correct action type such as receipt, due, concession, or reversal.
Enter the amount and reason carefully so the ledger stays auditable.
Save the entry and verify the outstanding balance updates correctly.
Use reversal only when correcting an already recorded wrong transaction.
documents.note: Clear notes make accounting and audits much easier later.

documents.title: What do Paid, Partial, and Pending mean in fees?

What is common configuration in fees?
How does student fee customization work?
How do receipts, dues, concessions, and reversals work?
Fee statuses
Partial fee meaning
Pending fee explanation
documents.answer: Paid means the current outstanding balance is fully cleared. Partial means some amount has been collected but balance still remains. Pending means the fee obligation is still open and needs collection or follow-up from the school.
steps: Review Total Fee, Paid, and Outstanding together.
Use the status pill only as a quick visual summary.
Post new transactions until the status reflects the actual balance.
documents.note: Outstanding balance is the final truth, not just the color or label.

Check Student Report for the same year and class.
Verify the students are present in year enrollment.
Return to Fee Management and confirm the class filter.

documents.answer: Choose the audience based on who truly needs the message. Whole-school notices should stay broad, class notices should stay class-specific, and parent-facing notices should be used only when the communication is meant for guardians rather than internal staff workflow.
steps: Use school-wide audience only for notices relevant to the whole institution.
Use class or section audience for academic or operational notices limited to one group.
Use parent audience when guardians must be informed or act on the update.
Recheck targeting before sending so the wrong audience does not receive the message.
documents.note: Wrong audience selection can create confusion quickly.
